domain_restrictions: m is a natural number (so m is nonnegative and m+1 is positive)
the expressions (m : ℕ) and (m + 1 : ℕ) indicate casting natural numbers into integers before forming z = ... and applying the unary minus
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For every integer z, there exists a natural number m such that either (1) z equals m when m is viewed as an integer, or (2) z equals minus (m+1) when m+1 is viewed as an integer.
quantifier_order: there exists m in natural numbers
witness_dependencies: the witness m is allowed to depend on the given z
implicit intended choice: if z is nonnegative then take m = z; if z is negative then take m = -z - 1

statement_nl: Every integer z satisfies: there exists a natural number m such that z = (m : ℤ) or z = -((m + 1 : ℤ)).
